chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Speak about the creation of God, but do not speak about God Himself; for speaking about God only increases its doer in bewilderment.
And in another narration from Hariz: Speak about everything, but do not speak about the Essence of God.

key_terms.الْكَلَام فِي اللَّه: Speech about/regarding God — speculative theological discourse about God's nature, attributes, or essence
key_terms.تَحَيُّر: Bewilderment, confusion, perplexity — the inevitable outcome of trying to define the indefinable
key_terms.خَلْق: Creation of God — the universe and all creatures that God has made; discussable because creation is observable and rational
key_terms.ذَات اللَّه: The Essence/Self of God — God's ontological being in itself, which transcends all human categories and language

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about speaking about God's essence?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) forbids speculative discourse about the Divine Nature (dhat Allah), while permitting discussion of God's creation. The hadith reflects the Shia theological principle of tawqif — halting before the unknowable — against Mu'tazilite and philosophical speculation about God's essence. The addition from Hariz broadens the prohibition: any attempt to define or describe God's 'dhat' (Self/Essence) leads only to confusion, not understanding.
word_analysis: its owner/the one engaged in it

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Abu Baseer who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You can speak regarding the creation of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, but do not speak regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for the speech regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not increase its owner except with the confusion’. 
And in another report, from Hareyz, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘You can speak regarding everythings, but do not be speaking regarding ‘ذَاتِ اللَّهِ’ the Essence (Self) of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir From Imam abu Ja‘ far (a.s.)

who has said the following. “Speak about the creation of Allah and do not speak about Allah His-self. Speaking about the Allah’s self does not increase anything to one’s knowledge except more confusion.”
In another Hadith from Hariz it reads, “Speak about every thing but do not speak about Allah’s self.”
